newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB, Bankers Trust say to consider mutual stakes.
newsitem.headline: NCB, Bankers Trust say to consider mutual stakes.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) and Bankers Trust New York Corp said on Friday they will consider a limited amount of mutual capital participation after NCB completes its capital restructuring.

The two banks said in a joint statement that they signed a memorandum of understanding concerning business collaboration earlier on Friday, encompassing areas including securitisation business, overseas financial business and support services.
NCB, a heavily indebted Japanese long-term credit bank, said earlier this month that it would tie up with Bankers Trust, and seek the U.S. bank's help in securitising some of its loans.
On April 1, NCB unveiled its restructuring plan under which it would terminate its overseas operations, sell prime real estate and float new shares to try to rebuild its capital base.
"The business collaboration combines the expertise of both parties to strengthen their securitisation business which is expected to further expand," the statement said.
The two banks have set up a working group which has started planning securitisation transactions of real estate and other assets with transaction sizes of 50-100 billion yen, the statement said.
As for its overseas business, NCB will set up a special division to coordinate its operations with Bankers Trust to effectively serve its clients.

Bankers Trust is also studying various ways to coordinate with its overseas offices to supplement this effort, the statement said. The two banks have already started discussing further details of the collaboration, it said.
